title: Prince William and Kate Meet Modi in Delhi as Three-Day India Visit Concludes
excerpt: The Prince and Princess of Wales closed their India tour with talks on trade and the new India-UK economic agreement, after a final Mumbai morning split between a Bollywood studio and a maternity hospital.
body:
• Prince William and Catherine met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Wednesday, closing a three-day visit to India built around the Earthshot Prize awards in Mumbai.
  • The two sides discussed trade and bilateral ties; Modi pointed to momentum from the recently implemented India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement.
  • On the final morning, William watched Bollywood dancers at Karan Johar's Dharma Productions while Catherine visited a Mumbai maternity hospital and a craft school.
  • It was the couple's first joint overseas tour in four years, and Catherine's most high-profile trip since her cancer treatment in 2024.

Prince William and his wife Catherine met Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Wednesday to discuss trade and the countries' bilateral ties, wrapping up a three-day visit to India, Reuters reported. The couple flew to the capital from Mumbai after a final morning of separate engagements in India's financial capital.

Modi praised the work of William's Earthshot Prize, which held its annual awards ceremony in Mumbai on Tuesday. A Kensington Palace spokesperson said the discussion reflected "on the deep and enduring ties between the two countries" and the opportunities ahead, and that the couple expressed gratitude for the exceptionally warm welcome they had received in India.

"Look forward to further strengthening the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and building on the momentum of the recently implemented Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, for the shared prosperity of the people of our nations and the wider world."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India, on X

A Bollywood final morning in Mumbai

Earlier on Wednesday, the couple carried out separate engagements. William visited the office of Dharma Productions, the Bollywood production house run by filmmaker Karan Johar, in suburban Mumbai, where he smiled and clapped as dancers performed a number from the studio's hit film "Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham," which is set partly in London. Actors Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan were also present, according to Reuters.

"He was gracious and kind and spoke extensively about the potential of Indian cinema and how cinema across all Indian languages is loved worldwide," Johar said after the visit. Catherine, meanwhile, visited a maternity hospital in central Mumbai to speak to health workers, and the couple also made traditional silk napkins during a visit to the Chanakya School of Craft, Hello Magazine reported.

Three days built around Earthshot

The visit began on Monday and mixed ceremony with sport and climate advocacy. The couple played cricket with retired Indian great Sachin Tendulkar, visited a craft school, and attended Tuesday's Earthshot Prize ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai, where five winners each received £1 million for environmental projects — among them India's Mahindra Last Mile Mobility.

In his speech at the ceremony, William said the impact of global warming was becoming conspicuous, pointing to repeated heatwaves and devastating floods, and called it a pivotal moment for the planet. He founded the Earthshot Prize six years ago.

Why it matters beyond the photographs

The Delhi meeting gave the tour a policy endpoint. The India-UK trade agreement Modi cited has only recently come into force, and both governments have framed it as the centrepiece of a closer economic partnership — one with direct stakes for the large Indian diaspora in Britain, from business travel and professional mobility to the cost of goods moving between the two countries. A royal visit does not negotiate any of that, but the Modi meeting signals that London and New Delhi want the relationship's momentum noticed.

The trip was also a personal milestone: Reuters noted it has been the most high-profile overseas visit for the Princess of Wales since she underwent treatment for cancer in 2024, and the couple's first joint overseas tour in four years.
